title: Last Ninja Remix
build: I-TAL/TSM release; Central Park in active play, one declared level
uncounted: loaded with the game, after scene_leaf_000 ($4DFA)

records.c: JMP $8361: the load coordinator jumps here ($1728, jmp $3FF3) once the play load is in, and this goes on to EngineEntry at $8361.
JMP $89CB: StartLevelLoad calls this ($1405, jsr $3FF6) before it loads the next part. Central Park's points at the machine set-up at $0E00; Final Battle's points at an RTS, so it does nothing.

The tune's restart flag: the interrupt routine restarts the tune (jsr $4000) when it finds this byte nonzero, clearing it first ($1EEE-$1EF8), and the title sequence clears it at $110D before it starts the tune. The six zero bytes after it, up to the music jumps at $4000, are read by no instruction.

Purpose: initialize Final Battle's retained SID music module. Inputs: A selects the song. Outputs: initialized music state. Assumptions: retained module and gameplay phase match. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and music state. Hardware changes: initializes state later emitted to SID.

Purpose: service one Final Battle music tick. Inputs: initialized sequencer state. Outputs: advanced tracks and SID register image. Assumptions: the retained module matches the active gameplay phase. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and music state. Hardware changes: writes SID registers.

Purpose: set Final Battle's three music-control bytes from A. Inputs: A is the control value. Outputs: updated player controls. Assumptions: module active. Clobbers: flags and music scratch. Hardware changes: none directly.

Purpose: increment Final Battle's music gate/pause state. Inputs: module active. Outputs: incremented gate byte. Assumptions: retained player state is valid. Clobbers: flags. Hardware changes: none directly.
101 bytes of text that nothing reads, carried with the tune: "MUSIC COMPOSED BY REYN OUWEHAND WHILE BEING BUGGED BY FALCO, RICHARD & JOHN! PLAYER/SOUNDS BY FALCO".

records.c: Purpose: implement Final Battle's retained music sequencer and track-bytecode parser. Inputs: song descriptor, three voice streams, and player state. Outputs: updated music/SID state. Assumptions: retained code and sequence tables are from the same level title. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and player state. Hardware changes: writes SID registers during tick service.

Purpose: Implement Level's $4006 music-control veneer by storing A into the module's three control bytes and returning.
Inputs: A is the control value; the matching retained music occupant and its writable state are active.
Outputs: A is stored to $4078-$407A; A, X, Y, and all status flags are preserved on return.
Assumptions: The three adjacent bytes are the control triplet for this exact music-module occupant.
Clobbers: Memory $4078-$407A; A, X, Y, and flags are preserved, and RTS advances SP by two over the caller's return frame.
Hardware changes: No hardware registers are written directly.

Purpose: copy A into the paired global music-control bytes. Inputs: A is the control value. Outputs: both control bytes equal A; A, X, Y, and flags are preserved. Assumptions: Final Battle music-player occupant is active. Clobbers: memory only. Hardware changes: none directly; the later music service consumes the state.

Purpose: Implement Level's $4003 music-tick veneer, honoring the module gate and advancing its sequencer and SID image.
Inputs: The module is initialized; $4073 is its gate byte and the resident IRQ enters through the matching $4003 veneer.
Outputs: Advances or gates the current music tick, updates sequencer/envelope state, emits the resulting SID register values, and returns.
Assumptions: The retained title/play music module matches the active phase and the call occurs at the engine's normal music-tick cadence.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, zero-page music cursors, module track/envelope state, and SID register state.
Hardware changes: Writes SID voice and filter/volume registers as directed by the current tick; no CIA or VIC-II access is introduced by the veneer body.

Purpose: Implement Level's $4009 gate veneer by incrementing the module gate byte and returning.
Inputs: $4073 is the writable gate byte for the matching retained music occupant.
Outputs: $4073 is incremented modulo 256; N and Z describe the new value; A, X, and Y are preserved.
Assumptions: The caller intentionally changes the module gate/pause state and accepts byte wraparound.
Clobbers: $4073, N, and Z; A, X, Y, C, V, D, and I are preserved, and RTS advances SP by two over the caller's return frame.
Hardware changes: No hardware registers are written directly.

Purpose: fetch and interpret the next note or effect command for a voice. Inputs: phase-local voice index, stream pointers, and player state. Outputs: stream cursors, note/effect parameters, and target-frequency state are updated. Assumptions: streams use the observed $FE/$FD control-token encoding. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, indirect-pointer scratch, and voice scratch. Hardware changes: none directly.

records.s: [offcut 4564] Self-modified immediate operand of `LDY #$00` at `$459E`. The Final Battle music sequencer writes the selected sequence index here at `$456C`; the following indexed table reads install the sequence pointer in `$FE/$FF`.

records.c: Loads the selected four-entry pitch-sequence pointer, reads the current per-voice cursor $40AD, handles $FD/$FE control and $FF redirection, updates frequency-high state $40BC, clears $40B9 and advances the cursor. The $45CD branch advances the cursor then restores the note frequency through $45FE. Uses the instrument-selected index embedded in the preceding LDY operand.

Purpose: advance a voice's auxiliary effect sequence. Inputs: selected voice and its auxiliary pointer and cursor. Outputs: the next auxiliary value or control state is installed. Assumptions: the pointer addresses a valid phase-local auxiliary sequence. Clobbers: A, Y, flags, cursor state, and voice scratch. Hardware changes: none directly.

Purpose: load a note's target frequency into the selected voice state. Inputs: note-table index and voice-state index. Outputs: target-frequency low and high bytes are updated. Assumptions: both indices are valid for the phase-local frequency tables. Clobbers: A, indexed voice state, and flags. Hardware changes: none directly; this routine does not write SID registers.

Purpose: move current pitch toward its target under the current pitch-step rule. Inputs: current and target frequency plus signed step state. Outputs: current frequency is stepped and clamped, with a next target loaded when required. Assumptions: the paired frequency bytes and step state are internally consistent. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and voice arithmetic scratch. Hardware changes: none directly.

Purpose: update one voice's pitch envelope for the current music tick. Inputs: voice index, envelope cursor, current frequency, and envelope stream. Outputs: frequency, cursor, and envelope counters are advanced. Assumptions: the active envelope pointer addresses a valid stream. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and voice scratch. Hardware changes: none directly.

Purpose: conditionally initialize one voice's modulation stream. Inputs: X selects the voice, Y selects its modulation definition, and the current per-voice guard controls initialization. Outputs: when the guard is zero, the modulation cursor and count are cleared and the definition's mode bit is installed; otherwise voice state is unchanged. Assumptions: X and Y index valid phase-local voice and definition records. Clobbers: A and flags, plus indexed voice state only on the initialization path; X and Y are preserved. Hardware changes: none directly.

Purpose: execute one modulation-stream step. Inputs: selected voice, modulation cursor and count, and current frequency. Outputs: cursor, count, and modulated frequency are updated. Assumptions: the stream follows the observed signed-update and control-token encoding. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and voice scratch. Hardware changes: none directly.
